title: Regression Scout Bulletin — biweek ending 2026-05-03
content:
Period covered: 2026-04-20 → 2026-05-03

Executive summary:
- Quality signal degraded across newly onboarded model family 'mistral-13b-quant' for low-context customer promptsets. Aggregate pass-rate (eval-suite v3) slid from 91.8% → 85.6% (absolute -6.2pp). Drift concentrated on instruction-following and enumeration tasks.
- Latency and infrastructure signals stable; no correlated GPU OOMs. Regression appears algorithmic (generation behaviour) rather than infra.
- Urgent: prioritize promptset-specific rollbacks and targeted prompt engineering for top-3 failure clusters. Aim for mitigation patch + canary within 72 hours.

Key telemetry (biweekly snapshot):
- Eval-suite v3 pass-rate (weighted): 85.6% (down from 91.8%)
- Top promptset cohorts impacted: customer-onboarded-forms (↓12pp), internal-chat-assist (↓8pp), search-reranker-synth (↓7pp)
- Median latency (token): 48ms (no change). 95th latency: 142ms (stable).
- Token-level log-loss delta vs baseline: +0.14 (worse)

Top failure signatures (ordered by severity × frequency):
1) Truncated enumerations — model returns partial lists or stops mid-item (2040 failures, +320 since last period). Example: "List steps to reset X: 1) ... 2) 3" → stops at 2.
2) Hallucinated dates — confidently invents future timestamps for past events (760 failures). Example: claims meeting occurred "2027-01-10".
3) Instruction-ignore on 'format-as-CSV' tasks — returns prose (450 failures).
4) Reranking inversion — higher-scored item demoted for short-context queries (380 failures).
5) Tokenization split artifacts — repeated subword fragments in token boundaries (210 failures).

Signal provenance and triage notes:
- Drift origin: majority of affected prompts share short-context length (<120 tokens) and required strict formatting. Suggests conditioning shift under shorter context.
- Canary traces show that longer-context variants (>=256) retain baseline behaviour, pointing to positional-kv interaction.
- No deploys to runtime in the window that would explain sudden change; model family update on 2026-04-18 (mistral-13b-quant v2) is the most likely candidate.
- Cross-checked with infra: no GPU memory churn, same kernel set as baseline.

Immediate mitigation plan (72h):
A) Emergency route: pin onboarding customers to model-variant 'mistral-13b-quant:v1' for affected promptsets. Owner: Sanjay Patel. ETA: 24h.
B) Hotfix prompt transforms: prepend "STRICT FORMAT: return CSV rows only" and add post-filtering for enumerations. Owner: Maya Liu. ETA: 48h.
C) Canary + instrumentation: deploy patch to 5% of traffic for internal-chat-assist cohort with detailed token-level trace. Owner: Ethan Brooks. ETA: 72h.
D) Longer-term: open investigation into KV-cache behaviour for short context sequences; attach microbench harness to reproduce. Owner: Rina Shah. ETA: 2 weeks.

Playbook (triage runbook steps when a new regression triggers):
1) Surface: alert from quality-signal (threshold breach). Create JIRA with 'reg-scout' label. (Already: ML-402)
2) Quick classify: sample 50 failing prompts, create signature buckets by failure type.
3) Check infra: correlate deploys, kernel changes, autoscaler events in +-48h window.
4) Reproduce locally with quantized-vs-fp variants; run token-trace to inspect early-stopping or EOS logits.
5) Immediate mitigation: pin or route to fallback model variant; deploy prompt transforms if pinned unavailable.
6) Postmortem: summarize root cause, owner, timeline, and follow-ups; feed tests to onboarding-eval harness.

Action item table (owners + due dates):
- Sanjay Patel: Implement variant pinning for affected customers (due 2026-05-05)
- Maya Liu: Patch prompt-transform library + unit tests for enumeration tasks (due 2026-05-06)
- Ethan Brooks: Add token-trace instrumentation to canary path and run 48h smoke (due 2026-05-07)
- Rina Shah: Repro harness for KV-cache/short-context failure (due 2026-05-18)
- Ava Martinez (me): Draft postmortem and add 8 canonical failing prompts to onboarding-eval (due 2026-05-10)

Open questions / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: quantization schedule in v2 introduces cold-start EOS bias in short contexts. Test: compare logits distribution near EOS between v1/v2 on small prompts.
- Hypothesis B: kernel selection fallback in certain GPUs changes attention normalization slightly. Test: force same kernel set and rerun.
- Do we need to expand eval-suite to include more short-context strict-format tests? Proposal: add 500 synthetic enumerations and 200 CSV-formatter checks.

Notes for customer success / comms:
- Prepare a concise status note for impacted customers: root cause under investigation, immediate pinning and prompt-transform mitigations, ETA for visible improvement 24–72h.
- Avoid overcommitting: use measured language and offer rollback as safe option.

Appendix: quick reproducibility CLI
- run_local_eval --model mistral-13b-quant:v2 --promptset enumerations-short --trace_tokens --out artifacts/trace_may04
- compare_logits.py artifacts/trace_v1.json artifacts/trace_v2.json --metrics eos_bias

Last checked dashboards:
- /dashboards/quality/eval-suite-v3 (snapshot id: 2026-05-04-qs)
- /dashboards/telemetry/token-loss-by-model (snapshot id: 2026-05-04-tl)

Quick links:
- Jira: ML-402
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rruntime/pull/1284
- Confluence: Onboard-Evals/Promptset-Hub

Notes to self (loose):
- If hotfix prompt transforms reduce throughput significantly we need to coordinate with infra for autoscale windows.
- Consider adding 'short-context strict' bucket to daily regression monitor.

End of bulletin.
